chapter.title: When it goes wrong: loops, made-up facts, and wrong turns

cards.body:
Picture the intern's notepad at 6pm. Every agent keeps one like it: a *log*, one line per step, saying what it tried and what came back.

When the intern goes wrong, it happens in exactly **3 ways**, and each leaves a different mark on that notepad: the same line copied 12 times, a result nobody actually handed them, or a neat answer to a question nobody asked.
cards.simpler:
Think of a helper who writes down every step of their day in a notebook. Every agent keeps one like it, called a *log*: one line per step, saying what it tried and what came back.

When the helper goes wrong, it happens in exactly **3 ways**. Each leaves its own mark on the page: the same line written 12 times, a result nobody actually gave them, or a tidy answer to a question nobody asked.

cards.prompt: The intern was asked to find the office printer's model number. Their notepad reads: 'Checked the supply cupboard. Not there. Checked the supply cupboard. Not there. Checked the supply cupboard. Not there.' Which kind of going-wrong is this?

options.text: Stuck in a loop, repeating a step that already failed
Made up a result nobody gave them

whyNot.b: That's the made-up fact, not this: every result here really came back from the cupboard. It just came back the same 3 times.
whyNot.c: That's the wrong turn, not this: the intern is still on the right task, the printer. They're just not moving.

cards.reteach: Look at what repeats. A loop shows up as the same action with the same result, line after line, with no new information between them. A healthy log changes a little every step.

cards.title: Two failures you can see in the log
cards.body:
An agent's log is the notepad: one line per turn, saying what the model asked for and what the tool sent back. Reading it is mostly about **spotting what should not be there**.

Failure 1 is the *loop*: the agent tries a step, it fails or gives nothing new, and the agent tries the exact same step again. And again. The clue is repetition with no change.

Failure 2 is the *made-up fact*: the model writes down a result that no tool returned. The clue is a fact appearing in the model's text with no tool line above it to explain where it came from.
cards.simpler:
An agent's log is that notebook. One line per turn, saying what the model asked for and what the tool sent back. Reading it is mostly about **spotting what should not be there**.

Failure 1 is the *loop*. The agent tries a step, it fails or brings nothing new, and the agent tries the exact same step again. And again. The clue is repetition with no change.

Failure 2 is the *made-up fact*. The model writes down a result that no tool returned. The clue is a fact in the model's text with no tool line above it to explain where it came from.

cards.title: The weather that never arrived
cards.body:
An agent was asked for tomorrow's weather in Lisbon. Step 1: it called the weather tool. Step 2: the tool returned 'service unavailable'. Step 3: the model wrote, 'Tomorrow in Lisbon will be 24 degrees and sunny, pack light.'

**Nothing above step 3** says 24, or sunny, or anything about Lisbon's sky. The agent did not look it up. It remembered what Lisbon usually feels like and served it with a straight face.
cards.simpler:
An agent was asked for tomorrow's weather in Lisbon. Step 1: it called the weather tool. Step 2: the tool answered 'service unavailable'. Step 3: the model wrote, 'Tomorrow in Lisbon will be 24 degrees and sunny, pack light.'

**Nothing above step 3** says 24, or sunny, or anything about Lisbon's sky. The agent did not look it up. It remembered what Lisbon usually feels like and said it with a straight face.

cards.prompt: You're reading a log. Step 4: the model asks the calendar tool for free slots on Friday. Step 5: the tool replies with an empty list. Step 6: the model says 'Booked you in for Friday at 3pm.' Which failure is step 6?

options.text: A loop: it keeps asking about Friday
A made-up fact: the 3pm slot came from nowhere
A wrong turn: it should have checked Thursday

whyNot.a: That's the loop, not this: nothing is repeated here. Each step is new. It's just that step 6 isn't backed by step 5.
whyNot.c: That's the wrong turn, not this: Friday was the right task. The problem is that 3pm appears with no tool line that produced it.

cards.reteach: For every fact the model states, look one line up. Is there a tool result that contains it? If the tool said 'empty' and the model said '3pm', the 3pm is invented.

cards.title: The quiet one: solving the wrong problem
cards.body:
Failure 3 is the *wrong turn*: every step works, every tool result is real, and the agent finishes something that was never the goal. It is the hardest to spot because the log looks healthy. Nothing repeats, nothing is invented.

The clue lives at the top. Re-read the goal line, then read the last line. Do they match? An agent asked to 'find the cheapest flight to Rome' that ends with 'found the fastest flight to Rome' took a wrong turn, usually at the step where it first wrote 'fastest'.

So the reading order is **top and bottom first**, then scan the middle for repeats and for facts with no source.

cards.body:
Dev read a 10-line log where the agent had cheerfully renamed 200 photos by date and signed off with 'all done'. The ending looked perfect, so Dev marked it a pass. The goal line said 'rename by location'.

Spot it by **never trusting a tidy ending**: check the first line against the last before you read anything else.
cards.simpler:
Dev read a 10-line log where the agent had happily renamed 200 photos by date and signed off with 'all done'. The ending looked perfect, so Dev marked it a pass. The goal line said 'rename by location'.

It is like checking a delivery by looking only at the wrapping. Catch it by **never trusting a tidy ending**: check the first line against the last before you read anything else.

cards.prompt: A friend says: 'My agent's log looks totally fine. Every step worked, no errors, no repeats. But the result is useless.' Which failure is most likely, and where do you look?

options.text: A loop; look for repeated lines
A made-up fact; look for results with no tool behind them
A wrong turn; compare the goal line with the final line

whyNot.a: That's the loop, not this: a loop leaves repeated lines, and your friend said there are none.
whyNot.b: That's the made-up fact, not this: an invented result usually sits on top of a failed or empty tool call, and your friend said every step worked.

cards.reteach: When the log is clean but the answer is useless, the steps were right and the destination was not. Read the goal, read the ending, and find the step where the agent started heading somewhere else.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body:
Agents fail in **3 ways**: they repeat a step forever, they state a result no tool gave them, or they neatly finish the wrong task.

Read the log top and bottom first, then scan the middle for repeats and for facts with no source.
cards.simpler:

cards.body: Next time a chatbot gives you a specific number or date, reply: **'where did that come from?'** Watch whether it points to a real source or quietly changes the number. That second one is a made-up fact, caught live.
cards.simpler: Next time a chatbot gives you a specific number or date, reply: **'where did that come from?'** Watch what happens. It will either point to a real source or quietly change the number. That second one is a made-up fact, caught live.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now read a 10-line agent log, point to the step where it went wrong, and name which of the 3 failures it is.
